lines.japanese: 冬の朝は誰だって辛いものだ。少しでも惰眠を貪ろう、なんて気になる。
lines.english: Winter mornings were painful for everyone. They made a person want to steal even one more moment of idle sleep.

lines.japanese: そこに社会的な時間の制約があったとしても、睡眠欲っていうのは現実よりよっぽど強い。
lines.english: No matter how sternly society constrained one’s time, the hunger for sleep was far stronger than reality.

lines.japanese: だけど、今朝の目覚めは快適だった。朝からグレタガルドのドラゴンにだって立ちむかえそうな気がする。
lines.english: Yet I had woken in perfect comfort that morning. I felt ready to face down even a dragon of Gretagard at this hour.

lines.japanese: 「我こそは黄金の鷹、聖騎士ホークなり！」
lines.english: “Behold! I am the Golden Hawk, the Holy Knight Hawk!”

lines.japanese: 布団の上に立って、エア大聖剣を掲げてみた。
lines.english: I stood on my bed and raised an imaginary holy greatsword.

lines.japanese: 僕の失敗はドアを閉めわすれていたことだ。空想癖の強い兄だと思われたかもしれない。
lines.english: My mistake had been forgetting to close the door. She might now think her brother had an overactive imagination.

lines.japanese: 一階に下りながら、腕をぐるりと回してみる。うん、気のせいじゃなくて、やっぱり体が軽い。
lines.english: On the way downstairs, I swung one arm in a broad circle. Yes. I had not imagined it. My body truly felt light.

lines.japanese: 普段ならずしりと重い頭も今朝はやたらクリアで、外の景色まで明るく見える。どうせなら、テストが始まる前にこのくらいすっきりしていれば良かったのに。
lines.english: Even my head, ordinarily heavy as stone, was extraordinarily clear. The world outside seemed brighter. If only I could have felt this refreshed before the exams began.

lines.japanese: 昨日は色んなことがあったから、眠りが深かったのかもしれない。疲れてぐっすり……とか。そんなことを考えてみた。
lines.english: Perhaps I had slept so deeply because so much had happened yesterday. Exhaustion had carried me into sound sleep... Something of that sort.

lines.japanese: そう、昨日はいろいろあった。初めて自分から学級委員らしい仕事をしたクラス会議。山科さんや針生さんとの交流。渡来さんとの会話。そして、卒業文集制作で同じ班になったこと。
lines.english: Yes, yesterday had held any number of things: a class meeting in which I had acted like a proper class representative on my own initiative for the first time; encounters with Yamashina and Hariu; a conversation with Watarai; and our assignment to the same graduation-anthology group.

lines.japanese: そうだ、今日からは実際に作業が始まるんだ。作業の量は多いからちょっと大変だけど、それだけ渡来さんや針生さんと一緒に居られる機会が増えるってことだ。
lines.english: That was right. The work itself began today. There was a great deal to do, and it would be difficult—but that also meant more opportunities to spend time with Watarai and Hariu.

lines.japanese: もしかしたらこんなに体が軽いのは、きのう一日が充実していたせいかもしれない。
lines.english: Perhaps my body felt so light because yesterday had been such a full day.

lines.japanese: 今日の朝食、小鳩との会話は発展性のあるものにしよう。僕は鼻息をひとつ吹きだして、居間への襖を開けた。
lines.english: At breakfast today, I would have a conversation with Kobato that actually went somewhere. I puffed one determined breath through my nose and opened the sliding door to the living room.

lines.japanese: 「海苔って外国ではブラック・ペーパーって言うんだって」
lines.english: “Did you know people overseas call dried seaweed ‘black paper’?”

lines.japanese: 「ふーん……」
「胡椒がブラック・ペッパーで、海苔がブラック・ペーパー。間違えないようにしないとね」
lines.english: “Pepper is ‘black pepper,’ and dried seaweed is ‘black paper.’ We’d better not mix them up.”

lines.japanese: 「うん、うん」
lines.english: “Mm-hm.”

lines.japanese: 今日の朝食は日本食だった。ほかほかごはんが盛られた茶碗に、醤油を多めに混ぜたとろろいも。
lines.english: Breakfast that morning was Japanese: a bowl heaped with steaming rice and grated yam generously seasoned with soy sauce.

lines.japanese: 相変わらず兄妹の会話は弾まなかった。でも“毎日”だもんな。
lines.english: Conversation between brother and sister had failed to bloom as usual. But the task did say “every day.”

lines.japanese: 僕にあと何日残されてるかは分からないけど、まだ先はある。今日は明日の会話に繋げるための布石程度に考えて、あんまり気負わないようにしよう。
lines.english: I did not know how many days remained to me, but there was still time ahead. I would regard today as no more than groundwork for tomorrow’s conversation and try not to place too much weight on it.

lines.japanese: 「明日の朝食はどうしようか」
lines.english: “What should we have for breakfast tomorrow?”
“What?”

lines.japanese: 「な、なにか変でした？　だった？」
lines.english: “W-was anything amiss? Was something wrong?”

lines.japanese: 「え、なにが」
lines.english: “What? Wrong with what?”

lines.japanese: 「今日の朝食……」
lines.english: “Today's breakfast...”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことないよ、美味しいよ。なんで」
lines.english: “Nothing was wrong. It's delicious. Why?”

lines.japanese: 「だって、明日の朝食のこと聞くから……」
lines.english: “Because you asked about tomorrow's breakfast...”

lines.japanese: 「聞くから？」
lines.english: “Because I asked?”

lines.japanese: 「今日はなにか変なのかと思って」
lines.english: “I thought there must be something strange about today's.”

lines.japanese: 「そんなことないよ。おれ、とろろ芋すきだしさ」
lines.english: “There isn't. I like grated yam.”

lines.japanese: 「あ、よかった」
lines.english: “Oh. Good.”

lines.japanese: 「うんうん、よかった」
lines.english: “Good, good. I'm glad.”

lines.japanese: これは明日の会話に繋がるんだろうか。いや、会話をしようという心構えが大事なんだ。
lines.english: Would this truly lead into tomorrow's conversation? No. What mattered was maintaining the resolve to converse.

lines.japanese: 渡来さんも言ってたじゃないか。当たって砕けるくらいの勇気はないのかって。
lines.english: Hadn’t Watarai asked whether I had even enough courage to go for it and crash and burn?

lines.japanese: 「あ、でも、明日はパン食もいいかなあ」
lines.english: “Though bread might be nice tomorrow.”
“Hm?”

lines.japanese: 「いや、二日間パン食が続いたから、今日はごはんで嬉しいんだけど、でもパンもいいよね」
lines.english: “No, I was happy to have rice today after two days of bread. But bread is good too, isn't it?”

lines.japanese: 「うん？」
lines.english: “Mm?”

lines.japanese: 「小鳩はどっちがいい？」
lines.english: “Which do you prefer, Kobato?”
“What...?”

lines.japanese: 「……そ、その日の気分？」
lines.english: “...I-it depends how I feel that day?”

lines.japanese: 「うん、朝になってみないとわからないよね」
lines.english: “Right. You can't know until morning comes.”

lines.japanese: こくん。
lines.english: A small nod.

lines.japanese: 振り出しに戻る。どうしよう、もう一度当たってみようかな。
lines.english: Back where we began. What now? Should I try one more time?

lines.japanese: うん、もう砕けたからいいか。続きは明日にしよう。
lines.english: No. I had already crashed and burned. The rest could wait until tomorrow.

lines.japanese: 僕は発展性のない兄の不甲斐なさを恥じて、せめてとろろ芋で粘ついたお椀を小鳩が洗わなくてもいいように、自分で台所へ運ぶことにした。
lines.english: I was ashamed of being such an incapable brother, unable to make a conversation go anywhere. At the very least, I would save Kobato the trouble of washing the bowl sticky with grated yam, so I carried it to the kitchen myself.

lines.japanese: 楽しい食卓って難しいな。
lines.english: A cheerful breakfast table was hard to manage.
